transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Please have a seat. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been getting kind of stuck on a scar on my wrist. I know it probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep thinking everyone’s looking right at it. Like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or self-conscious about the scar most of the time, even when you’re not in social situations?

Mostly it’s when I’m around people… church, or bridge. I know it probably doesn’t look as bad as it feels to me, but I get self-conscious, like their eyes go right to my wrist. I don’t know if it’s most of the time, but it does stay on my mind.

When you’re in social situations like church or bridge, do you worry that others might notice something else about your appearance or behavior that you’re not comfortable with, or is it mainly the scar that bothers you?

It’s mainly the scar. I don’t really think it’s other things… it’s just, when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad as I’m making it, but it feels like that’s the first thing they notice now.
Does this concern about your scar ever make you want to avoid going to church or playing bridge at all, or make you feel really distressed while you’re there?

Yes… sometimes. I’ve skipped a few choir and theater volunteer things because I get too caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t show. And I’ve been late turning in some bookkeeping work too, which is… not like me.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about the scar itself — like how it looks, how big or shaped it is — even when you’re not around other people?

Not so much when I’m by myself, I guess… I know it’s probably not as bad as I think. But when I’m going to church or bridge, I do keep thinking people are looking right at my wrist, like that’s the first thing they notice.
When you’re worried about the scar showing, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly — like checking it, covering it, or going over what people might think in your mind?

Yes… I suppose I do. Before I leave, I’ll look at my wrist in the hall mirror a few times, maybe change sleeves or put on a bracelet so it’s covered. Sometimes I ask my husband if it looks noticeable, though he always says it’s barely there.
Do you feel that the scar is a defect or flaw in your appearance that makes you feel seriously unattractive or abnormal?

I… I don’t know if I’d say seriously unattractive. It’s just… I know the scar probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Are there other parts of your appearance, besides the scar on your wrist, that you worry about in a similar way — like maybe your face, hair, or other body parts?
No… not really. I mean, I’m not thrilled with getting older, but I don’t dwell on my face or hair like that. It’s mostly just the wrist.
When you’re not in social situations, do you still find yourself preoccupied with how the scar looks, or is your concern mostly limited to when you’re around people?

Mostly when I’m around people, I think. At home I can forget about it more. But if I’m going to church or bridge, then… yes, I start thinking it looks worse than it probably does, and that everyone will notice it right away.

Do you feel that your concern about the scar has started to interfere with your life in any way beyond just church or bridge—for example, with work, relationships, or other activities you used to enjoy?

A little, I suppose. I’ve been late with some of my bookkeeping work because I get stuck trying to cover it or make it less noticeable before I leave.

And… I’ve skipped a few choir things, and some theater volunteer commitments. I don’t like admitting that, but I just get too caught up worrying people will see my wrist.
Would you say that the scar on your wrist is a major focus of your attention, to the point where it feels like you can't stop thinking about it, even when you're not around other people?

Not all the time, no. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, it sort of takes over. I know the scar probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me, but I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it… like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Do you feel self-conscious about the scar only in situations like church or bridge, or do you also worry about it in other social settings, like running errands or meeting new people?

Mostly church and bridge. I mean… that’s when I really feel it. I know the scar probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me, but in those settings I keep thinking people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice.
Do you worry about the scar mainly because you're concerned people might judge you negatively or think less of you in those social situations, like church or bridge?

I suppose that’s part of it, yes. I know it probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but at church or bridge I keep thinking people’s eyes go right to my wrist… like that’s what they see first now.
When you're at church or playing bridge, is your main concern that people will notice the scar and judge you negatively, or is it more about how the scar looks to you regardless of what others think?

I think it’s… both, a little. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people notice it right away. Like their eyes go straight to my wrist.

Is it mainly the thought of people noticing the scar during activities like church or bridge — where you’re in the spotlight or interacting closely — that bothers you, or is it more about the way the scar looks to you in general?

It’s more when I’m there with people, I think. Church, bridge… those sorts of places. I know the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me, but I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice now.

When you're worried about the scar showing at church or bridge, is your main concern that people will judge you negatively because of it, or is it more about how the scar looks to you regardless of what others think?

I guess it’s more that I feel people will notice it. I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me, but at church or bridge I keep thinking their eyes go right to my wrist… like that’s the first thing they see.
Is your worry about the scar mostly about how people might react to it when you're around them, or is it more about how it looks to you, even when you're alone?

Mostly when I’m around people, I think. I know the scar probably isn’t as noticeable as it feels to me, but at church or bridge I keep thinking everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist… like it’s the first thing they see.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) with a preoccupation focused on a perceived defect (scar on wrist) that is not observable or appears slight to others. The concern is circumscribed to one specific body part and causes significant distress and avoidance in specific social situations (church, bridge). There is repetitive behavior (checking, covering, reassurance seeking) and functional impairment in social and occupational domains. Social anxiety disorder (F40.11) was considered but ruled out as the concern is not about being judged generally in social situations, but specifically about the perceived defect on display.
